speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I understand your husband is presenting with bizarre and agitated behavior; to begin our assessment, please describe the specific behaviors he has exhibited and how long they have been occurring. Have there been any recent changes in his sleep, appetite, or substance use?

speaker: Patient
text: 26-year-old male. The patient has been demonstrating bizarre and agitated behavior for the past 6 weeks. He believes that he is being spied on by the NSA which is also controlling his mind. His wife adds that he has been increasingly withdrawn and intermittently depressed over the last 3 months. He was terminated from his job 4 weeks ago after he ceased attending work. Since his unemployment, he has been focused on creating a device to prevent people from controlling his mind.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for those details. Given his fixed belief that the NSA is controlling his mind and his specific plan to build a device to counteract this, have these delusions been present for the entire duration of his agitation, or did they develop after a period of normal behavior? Additionally, has he experienced any hallucinations, such as hearing voices?

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Schizophrenia, acute episode with prominent delusions of control and persecutory content. The clinical picture of a 6-week psychotic break with fixed false beliefs (NSA control), functional decline (job termination), and social withdrawal supports this diagnosis. Further evaluation of auditory hallucinations and family history is unnecessary for the initial working diagnosis.
